topic: Europa may hold twice Earth's ocean water
claim: Under its ice shell, Jupiter's moon Europa likely has a salty ocean holding about twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans.

beats.caption: Tiny moon, giant ocean
beats.vo: A tiny moon may hide twice Earth's ocean water.

beats.caption: Europa: 1/4 Earth's width
beats.vo: Europa is only one-fourth as wide as Earth. But under its icy shell, scientists think a salty ocean lies sixty to one hundred fifty kilometers deep.

beats.caption: Ice shell: 15-25 km thick
beats.vo: That shell is fifteen to twenty-five kilometers thick. Magnetic readings from NASA's Galileo spacecraft point to salty water underneath. Add it up, and Europa's ocean may hold double all of Earth's oceans.

beats.caption: Is anyone home? 3D models: NASA
beats.vo: NASA launched Europa Clipper in October 2024 to find out if that ocean could support life. Would you bet on life there?

sources.text: NASA Science, Europa Facts: https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-moons/europa/europa-facts/ (ocean 60-150 km deep, ice shell 15-25 km, one-fourth Earth's diameter, ocean may hold twice Earth's global ocean)
